title: ffmpeg: re-encode to h265 1080p
body:
ffmpeg -i input.mkv \
  -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a -map 0:s? \
  -c:v libx265 -crf 23 -preset slow \
  -vf scale=-2:1080 \
  -c:a copy -c:s copy \
  out.mkv

title: SQL window function: running total
body:
SELECT
  ts,
  amount,
  SUM(amount) OVER (
    PARTITION BY account_id
    ORDER BY ts
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS running_total
FROM transactions
ORDER BY account_id, ts;

title: Proxmox: passthrough a GPU to LXC
body:
## Steps

1. Identify the device on the host: `lspci -nn | grep -i nvidia`
2. Enable iommu in `/etc/default/grub` (`intel_iommu=on iommu=pt`), run `update-grub` and reboot.
3. In the LXC config (`/etc/pve/lxc/100.conf`) append:

   ```
   lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 195:* rwm
   lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:* rwm
   lxc.mount.entry: /dev/nvidia0 dev/nvidia0 none bind,optional,create=file
   ```

4. Restart the container and verify with `nvidia-smi`.

SQLite LIKE search vs FTS5
body:
## Why LIKE

For a single-user library at ~10k items, a `LIKE '%term%'` query on a
denormalised `search_blob` is fast enough (<5ms) and avoids the operational
weight of FTS5 (virtual tables, content shadow, rebuild on schema change).

## Trade-offs

- No bm25 ranking; we sort by `updated_at DESC`.
- No prefix-only fast path. Mitigated by short-query fallback to `title LIKE`.
- Adding a column is one ALTER + one trigger rewrite, vs. a virtual-table rebuild.

title: Dockerfile: multi-stage Go binary
body:
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags='-s -w' -o /out/app ./cmd/app

FROM alpine:3.20
RUN adduser -D -u 10001 app
USER app
COPY --from=build /out/app /usr/local/bin/app
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/app"]
